decisions.reason: As a newly launched but already separately presented add-on that supports the firm's project business, it likely meets a modest first-year aspiration well enough to be retained.

The digital-twin service is a plausible strategic adjacency, and with only one year of market experience a medium-sized firm with some slack would usually continue it while learning, despite uncertain early results.

A generic authentication and identity delegation service is likely to face strong competition and overlap with the firm's more GIS-specific identity offer, making it the most likely candidate for reallocation of resources if results fall short of aspiration.

An open GIS application development framework fits closely with the firm's core capabilities and ecosystem logic, so management would likely tolerate uncertain short-run returns and keep it on the market.

Because the GIS-specific identity and access service was explicitly highlighted at launch and is tightly linked to the firm's core GeoIT business, it is likely above internal aspiration or strategically important enough to retain.
